nodes.name: Midsummer daylight
nodes.desc: Near-continuous summer light drives a short, intense growing season, while the winters are dark and cold.

nodes.name: Vatnajökull ice cap
nodes.desc: Europe's largest ice cap by volume sits at the heart of the park and feeds the rivers, outwash plains and glacial lagoons around it.

nodes.name: Glacial meltwater
nodes.desc: Silty rivers and lakes fed by melting ice shape the lowlands, lay down outwash sands and feed the lagoon at the glacier edge.

nodes.name: Outwash sands and volcanic soil
nodes.desc: Young, nutrient-poor soils of glacial sand and volcanic ash that plants colonise slowly and that dead matter helps enrich.

nodes.name: Soil microbes and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, droppings and carcasses, returning nutrients to the thin soil.

nodes.name: Black crowberry
nodes.desc: A low evergreen heath shrub with black berries, widespread on Icelandic moors and eaten by reindeer, ptarmigan and snow buntings.

nodes.name: Bog bilberry
nodes.desc: A dwarf heath shrub whose leaves and berries are food for reindeer, ptarmigan and small birds.

nodes.name: Woolly willow
nodes.desc: A low, silvery willow of Icelandic heaths and river plains; willow shoots and buds are a staple for grazers and ptarmigan.

nodes.name: Alpine bistort
nodes.desc: A small tundra flower with edible leaves and bulbils, eaten by geese and ptarmigan.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting microscopic algae in the sea and glacial lagoon that feed small crustaceans and fish. General ecological knowledge.

nodes.name: Reindeer
nodes.desc: Introduced to Iceland in the 18th century, the East Iceland herd grazes heath and highland plants, with lichen a winter staple.

nodes.name: Pink-footed goose
nodes.desc: Breeds in the Icelandic highlands, using wetlands near the glacier, and eats tundra plants in summer. The Arctic fox is its main land predator.

nodes.name: Rock ptarmigan
nodes.desc: A hardy grouse that stays all year and eats shoots, buds, leaves and berries of heath plants.

nodes.name: Snow bunting
nodes.desc: A small songbird of rocky highlands and shores that eats seeds and berries of heath plants.

nodes.name: Non-biting midges
nodes.desc: Their larvae live in lake and river mud on algae and detritus, and are food for fish. General ecological knowledge.

nodes.name: Atlantic herring
nodes.desc: Tides carry herring from the sea into Jökulsárlón, where seals, terns and skuas feed on them.

nodes.name: Arctic char
nodes.desc: A cold-water fish of Icelandic lakes and rivers that feeds largely on insect larvae and other small invertebrates.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A clever omnivore and scavenger that takes carrion as well as berries and other plant food.

nodes.name: Arctic tern
nodes.desc: Nests near the lagoon in large numbers and dives for herring and other small fish.

nodes.name: Great skua
nodes.desc: Nests on the sands by the lagoon; it kills seabirds, steals fish from other birds and eats carrion.

nodes.name: Harbour seal
nodes.desc: Gathers at the mouth of Jökulsárlón, especially in winter, to hunt fish brought in by the tide.

nodes.name: Arctic fox
nodes.desc: Iceland's only native land mammal, a mostly bird-eating predator that also scavenges carcasses.
